name: Minty Green
lede: Minty Green is a bright, yellowish spring green listed in the CSS and X11 color sets, and a word for color that goes back to 1766 even though this exact hex is recent.

sections.title: A web-list green
sections.body:
Minty Green appears as a CSS/X11 keyword and on Wikipedia's color lists, and separately in the xkcd 2010 crowd survey, which is the earliest record of this exact hex, #0BF77D [1]. Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary traces a color word built on *mint* back to 1766, though not necessarily this bright a shade; the library's own [[mint|Mint]] entry is a softer, paler green [1]. At lightness 86 and chroma 87 in LCH it is one of the most saturated greens in the library [1].

Its nearest named neighbor is [[android-green|Weird Green]], 4.3 CIEDE2000 units away and read as duller and darker, followed by [[bright-light-green|Bright Light Green]] and [[bright-sea-green|Bright Sea Green]], both 5.6 units off [2]. The library separately logs Spearmint and Spring Green as near-duplicate crowd names, 1.1 and 1.7 units off [1]. The nearest gem comparison is common [[gem:malachite|malachite]], 7.2 units away [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive has a color this bright and saturated covering even 1% of its canvas, as photographed [4]. That is unsurprising: a green this vivid and light sits far outside the range aged pigments and varnish typically produce, and it describes our museum holdings, not painting as a whole [4].
